title: Connective module-sheaf hypercohomology in nonpositive degrees
statement:
Let $(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ be a ringed space [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism], with its site of opens and open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] in a common universe containing the opens and module values [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $E\in D(\mathcal O_Y)$ be an object of the unbounded derived category of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and suppose its cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] satisfy $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ for all integers $i<0$. Define $H^i(V,E)=H^i(R\Gamma(V,E))$ for each open $V$, where $R\Gamma(V,-)$ is unbounded derived evaluation at $V$, computed on K-injective representatives, followed by forgetting scalars [def-sfb-right-derived-functor, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Then $H^i(V,E)=0$ for every open $V$ and every $i<0$. Moreover there is a canonical isomorphism of abelian presheaves
$$\bigl(V\mapsto H^0(V,E)\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigl(V\mapsto\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^0(E))\bigr),$$
natural in $E$ among objects satisfying the stated vanishing. For $W\subseteq V$, this isomorphism intertwines the derived evaluation restriction with the section restriction of the cohomology sheaf. Thus the degree-zero hypercohomology presheaf is the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^0(E)$, including its value on the empty open. No upper cohomological bound, quasi-compactness, or scheme hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D66 (cohomology-lemma-vanishing-and-glueing), proof of (1), third and fourth sentences: connective derived sections

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=\Mod(\mathcal O_Y)$. It is abelian with enough injectives by [lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives], which applies to an arbitrary ringed space. The assumed vanishing places $E$ in the full subcategory $D^+(\mathcal A)$ by [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative], (1) with $n=0$, and (2): choose an integer-indexed complex $I$ of injective module sheaves, $I^r=0$ for $r<0$, and an isomorphism $\alpha:QI\xrightarrow{\sim}E$; $I$ is K-injective. The full-subcategory convention views $\alpha$ also in the unbounded derived category. This chooses a single complex on $Y$, before choosing any open.

For every open $V$, let $C_V^r=\Gamma(V,I^r)$, as an abelian group, with differential $\Gamma(V,d_I^r)$. The site of opens of $Y$ is small, so every complex of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules has a K-injective resolution by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; this is the standing hypothesis of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] for $F=\Gamma(V,-)$ followed by forgetting scalars, an additive functor $\mathcal A\to\mathrm{Ab}$, so $R\Gamma(V,-)$ is defined on all of $D(\mathcal A)$. The K-injective evaluation rule of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], followed by the given $\alpha$, identifies $QC_V$ with $R\Gamma(V,E)$. Each $C_V^r$ is zero for $r<0$: the zero module sheaf has zero section groups. Therefore the formula $H^i(C_V)=\ker d_{C_V}^i/\operatorname{im}d_{C_V}^{i-1}$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives $H^i(V,E)=0$ for $i<0$. This uses evaluation of the global K-injective $I$ on each open; it does not assume that evaluation preserves injectives.

source.place: Tag 0D66 (lemma-vanishing-and-glueing), proof of (1), connective derived-section calculation

proof.text:
Since $I^{-1}=0$, [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] identifies $\mathcal H^0(QI)$ with $Z=\ker(d_I^0:I^0\to I^1)$. The kernel is sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so its sections are exactly $\{s\in I^0(V):d_I^0(s)=0\}$. Since $C_V^{-1}=0$, these same cycles, without any quotient by nonzero boundaries, are $H^0(C_V)$. Thus define the desired isomorphism by
$$H^0(V,E)\cong H^0(C_V)\cong Z(V)\xrightarrow{\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^0(\alpha))}\Gamma(V,\mathcal H^0(E)).$$
For $W\subseteq V$, restriction sends a cycle $s$ to $s|_W$, still a cycle since $d_I$ is a sheaf morphism. Both kernel identifications send that cycle to that same section, and $\mathcal H^0(\alpha)$ is a sheaf morphism. Evaluation restriction on the K-injective model is precisely this chain map $C_V\to C_W$, so the displayed isomorphisms commute with the specified derived restrictions. They form an isomorphism of abelian presheaves.

source.place: Tag 0D66 (lemma-vanishing-and-glueing), proof of (1); modules.tex Section 01AF (section-kernels), sectionwise kernel formula

proof.text: To check canonicity and naturality, choose such models $(I,\alpha)$ and $(J,\beta)$ for $E,E'$ and a derived map $f:E\to E'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], the map $\beta^{-1}f\alpha$ is represented by a chain map $a:I\to J$, uniquely up to chain homotopy. The derived-functor comparison in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] computes $R\Gamma(V,f)$ by $\Gamma(V,a)$, and [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] computes $\mathcal H^0(f)$ by the induced map on the kernels. Both send a cycle $s$ to $a^0(s)$, proving the naturality square. Explicitly, if $a,b$ are homotopic then [def-pur-kinjective-complex] gives $a^0-b^0=d_J^{-1}h^0+h^1d_I^0$; this vanishes on $Z$ because $J^{-1}=0$ and $d_I^0|_Z=0$. The same equation holds on sections on every open. Taking $f=1_E$ and two choices of model proves choice independence; composition and identities follow from composition and identities of the representing chain maps. Finally the right-hand presheaf is the underlying abelian sheaf of $\mathcal H^0(E)$ by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Transporting its unique-gluing property along the presheaf isomorphism proves the last assertion. On the empty open every module sheaf has the zero group of sections by the empty-cover sheaf axiom, so the same calculation includes that value.
